analyst_view.overall: Benfica (2nd, 28 points, 30 goals for and 10 against) host Famalicão (10th, 13 points) on Monday night, four days after a 0-4 defeat at Viktoria Plzeň in the Europa League that ended a run of four wins; Marco Silva has rotated little through a crowded schedule. Fredrik Aursnes (thigh) is doubtful: Silva said on 25 Nov he is probably not ready for Monday, while Dia de Jogo says he may be; the numbers count him out, as well as Leandro Barreiro. Prestianni skipped the Plzeň trip with adductor fatigue, but Silva called it a precaution and expects him to be fine. Famalicão, under Ricardo Silva since late October (two wins, a draw and a 0-3 loss at Braga in four league and League Cup games), have not played since their cup exit at Paredes and arrive rested, with Rodrigo Pinheiro back from suspension; they have not won in 16 visits to the Luz, though meetings have been high-scoring. Miguel Nogueira referees, with his record (4.2 cards a game in 5 games) already in the numbers; the view stays at the numbers as nothing clearly points either way.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.8 for Benfica and 0.9 for Famalicão, already taking a little off Benfica for Aursnes and Barreiro and adding a little to Famalicão for their recent scoring. Benfica should react after the 0-4 in Plzeň, but they have had little rest, and a fresh Famalicão that has scored well away from home could punish a shaken defence; these pull in both directions, so I stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, 6.9 for Benfica, who have won plenty lately (42 in their last six, already counted). Benfica will have most of the ball against a side that has rarely got anything at the Luz, which is what the numbers expect, and nothing in the news changes either side's wide play, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, already taking 4.5% off for Miguel Nogueira's lowish record and a little off Famalicão for fewer recent bookings. There is no rivalry or special stakes; a Benfica side stung by Plzeň may play with more urgency, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, 16.8 for Benfica, already adding a little for Benfica's high recent volume and cutting Famalicão for their low one. A tired Benfica after a Thursday night in the Czech Republic and a rested Famalicão could even this out slightly, but Benfica also have reasons to start fast at home after a heavy defeat, so I stay at 24.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target and already add 7.8% to Famalicão because Benfica have conceded more on target than usual lately. Prestianni is expected to be available and Aursnes's absence is already counted, so I see nothing new for accuracy and stay at 9.2.
